newsitem.title: USA: Power surge on ConEd lines hits New York City.
newsitem.headline: Power surge on ConEd lines hits New York City.

text.p: New York City was hit by a power surge about 1156 EDT Friday when two main circuits operated by Consolidated Edison Co of New York (ConEd) briefly tripped off line.
"Two of our high voltage feeders in Westchester County opened up, causing a momentary voltage dip. These are both 345 kilovolt (kv) lines," said ConEd spokesman Richard Mulieri.
"We don't know what caused the breakers to trip, but they came right back up again. We have crews looking into it right now."
He said the surge also knocked out a transformer at the Eastview power substation in Westchester County, just north of New York City, but had no further details.
The surge was felt across ConEd's power grid, from the tip of Manhattan north to White Plains, causing lights and computer screens to flicker.
